function: Fusion DQN learns UAV trajectory, ground-node (GN) scheduling and transmit power (RLA); the ALO variant also picks the UAV receive beam from a codebook, maximizing collected data (pp. 3, 5).
system: UAV with 30 antennas receives from 20 single-antenna ground nodes, 50 m altitude, 80 MHz bandwidth, no RIS, carrier frequency not stated (p. 5).
method: Rainbow-style fusion DQN (dueling, noisy, double, prioritized replay) trained by reinforcement learning; RLA adds an SCA inner loop for beamforming, ALO is fully DRL (pp. 3, 5).
data_channel: Own multipath model: large-scale fading, array response, small-scale fading over C paths; agent trained by interacting with the simulated environment, no dataset (pp. 2-3).
test_conditions: Single simulated 1 km x 1 km area, K=20, M=30; results averaged over 10 runs; sweeps of antennas, GN power, GN count; no unseen condition stated (p. 5).
baselines: Learned: ALO based on double DQN (DDQN). Fixed: fixed beamforming selection (FBS). No earlier published UAV data-collection method is compared (p. 5).
metrics: Reward, sum data collection (SDC) volume, energy efficiency, Jain fairness index (Figs. 2-7, pp. 5-6).
complexity: Big-O order for RLA, including the SCA term O((KN)^3.5 log(1/eps)), and for ALO; no runtime or FLOPs reported (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "large-scale fading coefficient, C represents the number of multiple path components"; the paper defines its own multipath model and cites no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "the numerical results in Figs. 4, Figs. 5, Figs. 6, and Figs. 7 are the average values obtained from 10 simulations"; sweeps of antennas, power and GN count are shown, but the paper never states that a trained model is tested on a setting unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 5: "two benchmarks, i.e., the ALO algorithm based on double DQN (DDQN) and fixed beamforming selection (FBS)"; DDQN is a standard learned baseline and FBS a fixed non-learned one, both compared on the SDC volume (Figs. 3-6).
q4_support: p. 4: "the computational complexity of the RLA algorithm is" O(U N (L(KN)^3.5 log(1/eps) + ((2+K)G)^2 + g1^2 + g2^2 + G^2 + Xi + log zeta)); the ALO order is on p. 5.
q5_support: p. 5: "The main parameters are summarized as follows: the number of GNs K is 20"; the paper runs its own simulation and gives no code or data link, DOI or public dataset.
notes: Step 1: research letter, not a survey. The learned FDQN controls UAV trajectory and GN power (p. 3, action A[n] = (UAV distance, UAV direction, P[n])) and, in ALO, the receive beam from a codebook (p. 5), so a physical-layer decision is learned jointly with trajectory and scheduling and the above_phy check passes under the aerial-link rule. Receive beamforming in RLA is solved by SCA, not learned (p. 4). Area 6: power, resource and beam control of a UAV link. q3 is borderline: the DDQN benchmark is the ALO scheme with DDQN in place of FDQN (p. 5), and FBS is not described beyond its name; accepted as a standard-algorithm baseline and a fixed-beam baseline, reviewer to confirm. No comparison with an earlier published method. The PDF is the arXiv 2409.14521v2 preprint (p. 1).
